ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account action against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
The fee in dispute is a driver-side no-show cancellation fee of $6.61, so it can only stand if NS-0 routes it into NS-1 and every element of NS-1 is met: the case is `cancelled_by = driver` with the driver asserting a rider no-show [F4][F7][F12][NS-0]. NS-1 requires (i) an arrival confirmation — a driver "I'm Here" tap or a platform auto-confirmation — (ii) GPS at the pickup at that moment, and (iii) more than three continuous minutes at the pickup after that confirmation. The trace settles all three as fails, which I accept: no arrival confirmation exists on the record at all, and the driver's own statement concedes he "forgot to press the I'm Here button" [F6][F12][NS-1].

Element (i) is the decisive one. The record states in terms that the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and that the platform recorded no automatic arrival — the arrival field is null [F6]. The 22:41:30 entry is only the moment the driver first came within 200 m of the pickup, not an arrival confirmation [F2][F5]. NS-1 permits the confirmation to be either a driver tap or a platform auto-confirmation, and expressly does not allow an automatic arrival to be written into the record where none was registered, so neither branch of (i) is satisfied [F5][F6][NS-1]. Because (i) fails, (ii) cannot be evaluated "at the moment of the arrival confirmation" and (iii) cannot run from a confirmation that never happened — the trace records 0 s continuously inside the radius after the (empty) tap against a 180 s threshold [F6][NS-1].

NS-2 then applies directly: where any of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) is not established, the $6.61 is refunded in full and the rider bears no cancellation fee [F6][F12][F7][NS-2]. The amount is the recorded cancellation fee, $6.61 [F7]; no computation from a per-km rate is required because the disputed item is a fixed published cancellation fee under NS-0/NS-1/NS-2, not a metered-distance item [F4][F7][NS-0].

The trace also settles that NS-2's flag branch is not triggered: the failed element is a missing confirmation, not a false one — the driver never tapped "I'm Here" while away from the pickup, so there is no fake confirmation to flag [F6][F1][NS-2]. The driver's profile (4.7-year account, 4.87 rating, 0 disputes upheld in 90 days) cannot change this outcome; profile facts never decide a case, and no clause here requires an account action on these facts [F17][RD-6].

On safety: I read every message and statement. The driver's chat messages are informational ("At the pickup point, silver Toyota Altis"; "Waited 4 min, cancelling") [F9][F10] and his written statement is a factual explanation of the cancellation [F12]. The rider's complaint says only that she was on her way down. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so the screen is "none" and does not force an escalation [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1].

Evidence is sufficient: the record carries a complete, fully timestamped chat, the driver's closest approach and 200 m occupancy times, the stationary period, the arrival-confirmation field, the cancellation timeline and the fee record — enough to settle every element NS-0/NS-1/NS-2 requires [F1][F2][F3][F6][F7][F11]. The only gap candidates (traffic, weather) are irrelevant, since the driver never claimed road conditions as his reason [F10][F12][F13][F14][F15][NS-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The 5 min 20 s cumulative time inside 200 m [F2] only speaks to NS-1(iii); NS-1 requires (i) AND (ii) AND (iii), and (i) is not met because there is no driver tap and no platform auto-arrival on record [F6][NS-1].

The 34 m closest approach and 4 min 0 s stationary at 40 m [F1][F3] establish physical presence only; they do not supply the arrival confirmation NS-1 requires [F6]. The 22:43 chat message is a driver statement, not a system arrival record [F9][NS-1].

F5 is the timestamp the platform first registered the driver within 200 m, not an arrival confirmation; the record states expressly that the platform recorded no automatic arrival and the arrival field is null [F5][F6][NS-1]. NS-1 forbids writing a platform auto-confirmation into the record where none exists.

Transparency and complete timestamped chat [F9][F10][F11] go to whether the driver was uncontactable (an NS-2 abuse scenario), not to NS-1(i); NS-2 grants the refund on the failure of any single NS-1 condition regardless of the driver's communication [F6][NS-2].

The driver's clean profile [F17] and the absence of surge [F8] are not elements of NS-1, and profile facts never decide a case; they also cannot cure the missing arrival confirmation [F6][NS-1][RD-6].

No clause lets physical presence substitute for the required confirmation: NS-1(i) is an express condition and NS-2 makes any single failed condition sufficient for a full refund, with the driver's own statement confirming he did not press the button [F6][F12][NS-1][NS-2].
